# Sirach Chapter 33 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 33 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 33 moves from the fear of the Lord (vv. 1–3) through memorable aphorisms about fools (vv. 4–6), the divine differentiation of days and human beings (vv. 7–15), Ben Sira's autobiographical aside (vv. 16–18), advice on retaining authority in old age (vv. 19–23), and instruction on managing slaves (vv. 24–33). The famous "potter and clay" image (v. 13) is close to Isaiah 29:16 and 45:9; Ben Sira applies it to social differentiation, not election theology. The passage on slavery (vv. 25–28) reflects ancient Hellenistic norms; translators should render accurately without anachronistic softening or harsh editorializing. Verse 30 ("treat him as a brother") introduces a countervailing humane note.

---

33:1 No evil will befall the man who fears the Lord, but in trial he will be rescued time and again.

33:2 A wise man will not hate the law, but one who acts hypocritically toward it is like a ship in a storm.

33:3 A sensible person will trust in the law, and for him the law is as reliable as a divine oracle.

33:4 Prepare what you will say and you will be heard; bind together your learning and then give your answer.

33:5 The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel, and his thoughts like a spinning axle.

33:6 A sarcastic friend is like a stallion horse; he neighs under everyone who mounts him.

33:7 Why does one day excel another, when all the daylight throughout the year comes from the sun?

33:8 They were distinguished by the Lord's wisdom, who made the seasons and festivals different from one another.

33:9 Some of them he exalted and hallowed, and some of them he made ordinary days.

33:10 All human beings come from the earth, and Adam was formed from the ground.

33:11 In the fullness of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them and made their paths different.

33:12 Some of them he blessed and exalted; some he set apart and drew near to himself; some of them he cursed and humbled, and drove them out from their station.

33:13 Like clay in the hand of the potter — to be shaped in whatever way he pleases — so human beings are in the hands of their Maker, to be treated as he determines.

33:14 Good is the counterpart of evil, and life the counterpart of death; so the sinner is the counterpart of the godly.

33:15 Consider all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, each one the opposite of the other.

33:16 I too was the last to keep watch, like one who gleans after the grape-gatherers; by the Lord's blessing I advanced, and like a grape-gatherer I filled my wine press.

33:17 Consider that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.

33:18 Hear me, you leaders of the congregation, and you rulers of the assembly, give ear.

33:19 Do not give authority over yourself to son or wife, brother or friend, during your lifetime, and do not give your property to another lest you regret it and have to ask for it back.

33:20 As long as you are alive and have breath in you, do not let any person take your place.

33:21 For it is better that your children should be dependent on you than that you should look expectantly toward the hands of your sons.

33:22 In all your activities keep the upper hand; let no blot come upon your honor.

33:23 When the days of your life reach their end, at the time of death, distribute your inheritance.

33:24 Fodder and a stick and burdens for a donkey; bread and discipline and work for a servant.

33:25 Set your servant to work and you will find rest; leave his hands idle and he will seek his freedom.

33:26 A yoke and a strap will bow the neck; for a malicious servant there are racks and tortures.

33:27 Assign him work so that he does not remain idle; for idleness teaches great mischief.

33:28 Set him to work as is fitting for him, and if he does not obey, make his chains heavier.

33:29 But do not be excessive toward anyone, and act with discernment.

33:30 If you have a servant, treat him as yourself, for you have need of him as of your own life.

33:31 If you ill-treat him and he runs away, on what road will you seek him?

33:32 There is a path through shame, and there is a path through honor; and the upright will find the way.

33:33 My soul takes pleasure in wisdom's teaching, and I speak of it without embarrassment.
